title.bn: পয়েন্টার দিয়ে singly linked list বানানো

summary.en: Insert, search, remove and free singly linked nodes while preserving ownership and handling empty-list boundaries.
summary.bn: নোড যোগ, খোঁজা, মুছে ফেলা ও free করার সময় পয়েন্টারের সম্পর্ক এবং খালি list-এর সীমা ঠিক রাখো।

sections.title: Join separately allocated boxes into an ordered chain
Represent a node and identify the incoming link
Exercise normal changes and boundary rejections
Unlink a node before releasing it
Read the chain and release the entire chain
Choose the structure for its operations
Test transitions rather than only long lists
Change one edge while preserving the rest

examples.title: Insert at the head, tail and a middle link
examples.explanationHtml: Each successful insertion redirects one incoming link. Positions are zero-based: inserting at the current length appends. The search reports the first matching position without modifying the list, and cleanup releases all four allocated nodes.

examples.title: Delete the middle, head and final node safely
examples.explanationHtml: The predecessor link is redirected before the removed node is freed. Removing the only remaining node updates head to null. A later removal returns failure without dereferencing null or changing ownership.

examples.title: Reject a position beyond the end without losing the existing list
examples.explanationHtml: A one-node list permits insertion at zero or one, not two. Validation finishes before allocation and mutation. The failed search leaves its output parameter unchanged. clear_list also resets the owning head, making repeated cleanup safe for that owner.

practice.title: Build and print a bounded list
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 through 8, then n integers from -100 to 100. Append in input order and print value -> for each node, followed by NULL. Missing or invalid input prints invalid after releasing any nodes already built. Allocation failure returns a failure exit status. All tokens fit int.
hints: The next tail insertion position is the current count.
Cleanup is required on input failure too.

practice.title: Remove one indexed node from a known list
practice.statementHtml: Read an integer position from -100 to 100. Build {10,20,30}; remove that zero-based position if it exists, then print the remaining list. Invalid positions print invalid. Always release the list. A missing input token also prints invalid.
hints: Reject negative input before converting to size_t.
A failed removal leaves the original list intact.

practice.title: Trace the order of link updates during insertion
practice.statementHtml: Draw insertion of 25 between nodes 20 and 30. Explain why setting the predecessor first can lose the suffix.
hints: Save the old successor in the new node before redirecting the predecessor.
practice.answerHtml: Before: 20 → 30. Set new.value to 25 and new.next to the existing 30 node. Then set the incoming link from 20 to new. After: 20 → 25 → 30. If the predecessor is redirected first and the old successor was not saved, reading that link no longer recovers the original suffix.

practice.title: Explain why free must follow saving the successor
practice.statementHtml: A cleanup loop frees node and then reads node->next. Repair the order and discuss aliases.
hints: Released storage is no longer a source of valid member values.
practice.answerHtml: Read next = node->next while node is live, free node, then advance to next. At the end set the owning head to null. Any borrowed pointer to a removed node becomes invalid and must not be dereferenced. Nulling the owner does not repair other dangling aliases.

quiz.prompt: Which value represents an empty list in this design?
options: A node with next pointing to itself
quiz.explanation: No dummy node is used here.

quiz.prompt: Why does insert_at receive struct Node **head?
options: Because int values need two bytes
It may replace the caller’s head pointer
quiz.explanation: Insertion at position zero changes the owning pointer.

quiz.prompt: Which assignment must happen before redirecting an incoming link to new?
quiz.explanation: Preserve the suffix before publishing the new node.

quiz.prompt: What must be saved before freeing a node during traversal?
quiz.explanation: Reading node->next after free is a use-after-free.

quiz.prompt: Which insertion positions are legal for a length-three list?
quiz.explanation: Position three appends; larger positions have no incoming link in this list.

quiz.prompt: What happens to a borrowed pointer to a deleted node?
options: It automatically points to the successor
quiz.explanation: Freeing storage does not rewrite all aliases.

quiz.prompt: What is the worst-case search time for n singly linked nodes?
quiz.explanation: A missing value can require visiting every node.

quiz.prompt: Which value is reached by one next link in a two-node chain?
quiz.explanation: The head next pointer names the tail node holding twenty.

quiz.prompt: What does redirecting the owning head select?
quiz.explanation: The pointer moves to last; these automatic nodes are not freed.

quiz.prompt: How many nodes are visited before the null terminator?
quiz.explanation: The loop visits a and b, then stops before dereferencing null.

keyPoints.en: Each live node owns a value and a link to the next node.
keyPoints.bn: প্রতিটি live নোডে একটি মান ও পরের নোডের link থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Redirect an incoming link only after preserving its old successor.
keyPoints.bn: আগের successor ধরে রাখার পর incoming link নতুন নোডে ফেরাও।

keyPoints.en: Deletion unlinks a node before releasing its storage.
keyPoints.bn: নোড মুছতে আগে chain থেকে সরাও, তারপর তার মেমরি free করো।

keyPoints.en: Empty, first, middle and last positions need explicit boundary reasoning.
keyPoints.bn: খালি list, প্রথম, মাঝের ও শেষ position আলাদা করে যাচাই করো।

keyPoints.en: Free the whole list on both success and abandoned construction paths.
keyPoints.bn: সফল কাজ ও মাঝপথে থেমে যাওয়া—দুই ক্ষেত্রেই বানানো list free করো।

examQuestions.question: Draw insertion at head, middle and tail for a singly linked list.
examQuestions.answerHtml: At the head, new.next takes the old head and head becomes new. In the middle, new.next takes the successor and the predecessor link becomes new. At the tail, the incoming null link becomes new and new.next is null. Allocate and initialise before redirecting any existing link. The supplied insert_at unifies these cases with a pointer to the incoming link.

examQuestions.question: Describe deletion of the only node and explain the ownership result.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The incoming link is head. Save the node, assign head from its next pointer (null), then free the saved node. The list is now empty and owns no allocation. A later removal fails without dereference. Borrowed aliases to the removed node are invalid even though the owning head was reset.

examQuestions.question: Compare an array with a singly linked list for indexed access and head insertion.
examQuestions.answerHtml: An array supports constant-time indexed access and contiguous storage. A singly linked list reaches an index by following links, taking linear time in the position. Head insertion needs constant link work after allocation, without shifting all existing values. Lists pay allocation and pointer overhead and often have worse locality. Choose based on the required operations, not a claim that one structure is always faster.
